## Observation

`.github/llm-providers/openai.toml` maps the openai arm's `trivial` class to `openai-responses:gpt-5.4-nano`. OpenAI's deprecations page (`https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations`, read 2026-11-11) lists `gpt-5.4-nano` / `gpt-5.4-nano-2026-03-17`, announced 2026-10-01, shutdown Apr 1, 2027, replacement `gpt-6-luna`. After shutdown every trivial-class call in the arm fails. `.github/llm-providers/README.md` and `docs/ci-provider-matrix.md` §"OpenAI arm model choice" still describe nano as the current trivial model.

## Root cause

The overlay pins a model id with no check that it is still current; nothing in the tree records OpenAI's deprecation.

## Choice of replacement

**`gpt-5.4-mini`.**
- It is not on the deprecations page and is listed on the catalogue; it is already the arm's `standard` model, verified on the repository's OpenAI account on 2026-08-03 and exercised by every openai arm run since.
- The pinned `pydantic-ai-slim` 1.107.9 gives it the same OpenAI profile as `gpt-5.4-nano` (measured: `supports_json_schema_output`, `supports_thinking`, `openai_supports_reasoning`, `openai_supports_sampling_settings` all True, no unsupported settings), so the request shape is unchanged.
Rejected:
- `gpt-6-luna`, OpenAI's named replacement: the pinned profile treats it as non-reasoning (`openai_supports_reasoning=False`, `supports_thinking=False`, measured), the same wrong-request-shape reason the docs already give for rejecting the GPT-6 family; recognition needs `pydantic-ai-slim` 2.x.
- `gpt-5.5`: the frontier model; a trivial slot gains nothing from it.

## Approach

1. `.github/llm-providers/openai.toml`: `trivial = { model = "openai-responses:gpt-5.4-mini" }`; update the header comment.
2. `docs/ci-provider-matrix.md` §"OpenAI arm model choice": record the 2026-11-11 move, the deprecation source and shutdown date, and the `gpt-6-luna` rejection; fix the estimate footnote's model list wording.
3. `.github/llm-providers/README.md`: state the trivial slot's model.
4. `tests/unit/test_ci_provider_matrix.py`: add the regression test below.
No config key, env var or flag.

## Scope

- `.github/llm-providers/openai.toml`
- `.github/llm-providers/README.md`
- `docs/ci-provider-matrix.md`
- `tests/unit/test_ci_provider_matrix.py`

## Testing

- RED then GREEN: a test reads every class slot and the scalar model in `openai.toml` and asserts (a) none is an id OpenAI has announced as deprecated, from a module-level table citing the deprecations page (currently `gpt-5.4-nano`), and (b) each id's pinned `openai_model_profile` has `openai_supports_reasoning` True, so a non-reasoning-profiled replacement cannot slip in. It fails on the pre-fix tree on (a).
- The existing `test_the_openai_arm_is_live_ready_with_its_own_credential` stays green.
- After merge, dispatch `Live External Integration` on `main` and check the openai job's usage log shows `gpt-5.4-mini` trivial-class calls completing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A test that fails on the pre-fix tree rejects a deprecated id or a non-reasoning-profiled id in any openai overlay slot.
- [x] `openai.toml`'s `trivial` slot is `openai-responses:gpt-5.4-mini`, and no tracked file names `gpt-5.4-nano` as a current model.
- [x] `docs/ci-provider-matrix.md` records the replacement, its source and date, and the rejected `gpt-6-luna`.
- [x] [non-codebase] A `Live External Integration` dispatch on `main` after the merge runs the openai arm with the new trivial model, recorded as a comment with the run id and the trivial-class call outcome.
  provenance: environment=GitHub Actions Live External Integration on main; principal=repository OPENAI_API_KEY secret; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — workflow_dispatch run and its usage-log artifact
- [x] [non-codebase] `env -u JIRA_URL -u JIRA_USER -u JIRA_API_TOKEN make verify` exits 0 on the commit pushed for review.
  provenance: environment=macOS dev host, fix-tamarin worktree; principal=Rebar Bot Nava; privilege_posture=narrower; instrument=live-call — exit status and log live outside the repository
